**A FUNK PERSPECTIVE ON BILLIARDS, PROJECTIVE GEOMETRY AND MAHLER VOLUME**

*DMITRY FAIFMAN*

42 pp, 20 sections.

**Abstract.** We explore connections furnished by the Funk metric, a relative of the Hilbert metric, between projective geometry, billiards, convex geome- try and aﬃne inequalities. We ﬁrst show that many metric invariants of the Funk metric are invariant under projective maps, as well as under projective duality. These include the Holmes-Thompson volume and surface area of con- vex subsets, and the length spectrum of their boundary, extending results of Holmes-Thompson and ´Alvarez Paiva on Sch¨aﬀer’s dual girth conjecture. We explore in particular Funk billiards, which generalize hyperbolic billiards in the same way that Minkowski billiards generalize Euclidean ones, and extend a result of Gutkin-Tabachnikov on the duality of Minkowski billiards. We next consider the volume of outward balls in Funk geometry.

**Outline.** Front matter; 1 Introduction; 1.1 Funk and Hilbert metrics; 1.2 Summary of results; 1.3 Plan of the paper; 1.4 Acknowledgements; 2.2 Projective geometry; 2 Preliminaries; 2.1 Convexity; 3.1 The projective co-nomadic Finsler structur; 2.3 Finsler geometry; 3 A projective outlook on the Funk metric; 3.2 The volume in Funk geometry; 4 Funk billiards and duality; 5 Integrability of Funk billiard in conics; 6 Schäffer's dual girth conjecture; 7 Mahler volumes of every Funk scale; 8 Maximizing the Funk-Mahler volume
